chunks.content: ## Adding and Managing Name Lines in CLO This section explains how to add, edit, and customize name lines in CLO, including different tools for adding name lines, positioning methods, and the use of the attribute editor for detailed adjustments. ### Adding Name Lines - Open the project file and add a name line for the model using the Cloud Library, which provides several standard name line styles. - Preview available name lines by clicking the preview icon. - To add a name line, double-click it in the library or drag it into the object window. - Use the toolbar’s name line tool to add name lines directly on the garment: - Position the mouse wheel on the garment's edge (inside or outside line). - Left-click to place the name line; multiple clicks add multiple lines. ### Name Line Tools There are three types of name line tools accessible by long-pressing the name line tool button: 1. **Line Name Line**: Adds a straight name line. 2. **Free Name Line**: Allows freeform drawing of the name line. 3. **Sewing Line Name Line**: Automatically creates a name line that follows a sewing line. ### Using the Free Name Line Tool - Select the free name line tool. - Choose a name line from the object window. - Position the mouse on the garment edge; a blue dot will appear. - Click and drag along the edge to create the freeform line. - Click again to finish. ### Using the Sewing Line Name Line Tool - Select the sewing line name line tool. - Sewing lines appear in the 2D window. - Hover over a sewing line; blue points appear. - Click and drag along the sewing line to create the name line. - Click again to complete. ### Editing Name Lines - The newly created name line is highlighted in bright red in the 2D window. - At garment corners, intersections may appear; use the free name line tool to avoid intersections. - Use the edit name line tool to delete or modify name lines. - Hold Shift to select multiple name lines and right-click to delete. - Adjust length by dragging the end points. - Move name lines by selecting and dragging. - The attribute editor shows properties of the selected name line, allowing type changes (e.g., from text to OBJ). ### Advanced Editing and Customization - Drag name lines in the object window to replace existing name lines on the 2D board. - Extend name lines beyond garment edges by opening the start or end points. - Corner curves can be set to rounded or right-angle shapes. - Smoothness settings allow natural, continuous extension at edges. - Adjust vertical distance (Z-axis) between the name line and garment panel. --- ## Customizing Name Line Properties This section covers how to define and customize the design, specifications, and materials of name lines, including pattern selection, stitching density, and display options.

Sewing line sewing wrinkles - Adding and deleting sewing wrinkles uses the same methods as name lines. ### Adding Sewing Wrinkles - Sewing wrinkles appear in dark purple when selected. - After adding, the object window switches to the sewing wrinkle column. - Select the default sewing wrinkle to edit. ### Customizing Sewing Wrinkle Properties - Rename the sewing wrinkle in the attribute editor. - Choose fabric material from options: cotton, dining cloth, leather, nylon, Dylen. - Select the sewing wrinkle type corresponding to the fabric (e.g., leather). - Apply different patterns and change color. - The hairline color is blue; adjust hairline strength to enhance wrinkle visibility. - Transparency settings control the wrinkle pattern’s opacity. - Adjust density to control wrinkle concentration; changes are visible in the 3D window. - Set the width of the sewing wrinkle. ### Editing Sewing Wrinkle Position and Length - Use the sewing wrinkle tool to select specific wrinkle sections. - Selected sections highlight in purple. - Adjust length and position by dragging, similar to name line editing. - In the attribute editor, extend wrinkle start or end points to 2D panel lines. - Adjust distance between wrinkles and include or exclude wrinkle width from the fabric. - Vertical distance from the panel can be adjusted using Z-axis settings. ### Saving Sewing Wrinkles - After finishing, save the sewing wrinkle: - Select it in the object window. - Click Save in the attribute editor. - Sewing wrinkles are saved in PTP file format for reuse. --- This document covers practical procedures and settings for adding and customizing name lines and sewing wrinkles in CLO, providing detailed guidance on tools, editing, material options, and saving formats for effective garment design enhancement.
